Simplified supply chain diagram for monocrystalline silicon ingot and wafer production 2.5.1 Technology Trends for Ingots and Wafers Most PV ingots and wafers were multicrystalline until 2017, after which monocrystalline wafers quickly became dominant, due in part to higher-efficiency monocrystalline cell technologies (Fischer et al. 2025). Until 2022, monocrystalline cells primarily used p-type wafers, which cost less than their n-type counterparts. However, n-type cells can be more efficient than p-type cells, and automation, improved dopant control, and larger ingots have reduced n-type wafer costs. For this reason, n-type monocrystalline wafers are projected to have greater than 90% global market share beyond 2025 (Fischer et al. 2025). PERC cells based on p-type wafers continue to represent a significant portion of U.S. imports and domestic production (see Section 2.4.1).
